answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a licensed comet-watch post on a named harbor jetty, where the holder must log a comet's passage on pigment-marked glass plates verified in person by an astronomy society steward. One observer cannot staff two jetties on the same night, and the steward visits one post per night, so no bulk buying is possible. The registration fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real jetty post, another night of observation, another human, and twice the prior fee.
